name: MineRL BASALT
description: We held the first-ever MineRL Benchmark for Agents that Solve Almost-Lifelike Tasks (MineRL BASALT) Competition at the Thirty-fifth Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2021). The goal of the competition was to promote research towards agents that use learning from human feedback (LfHF) techniques to solve open-world tasks. Rather than mandating the use of LfHF techniques, we described four tasks in natural language to be accomplished in the video game Minecraft, and allowed participants to use any approach they wanted to build agents that could accomplish the tasks. Teams developed a diverse range of LfHF algorithms across a variety of possible human feedback types. The three winning teams implemented significantly different approaches while achieving similar performance. reputation: A well-known MineRL competition benchmark in embodied RL and Minecraft agent research, with strong recognition from the NeurIPS community.
notes: Open-ended Minecraft tasks with natural-language instructions; evaluation can be noisy and implementation-dependent, and scores are not directly comparable across all task variants.
